evidence_quotes.quote: This paper presents a comparative analysis of specific aspects of concession agreements for water supply and sewage collection and treatment services in four Brazilian counties, undertaken in recent years, within the context of overcoming the legal model instituted by Planasa as of the 1970s.
The contracts were analyzed about permission payment, tariffs, coverage and investment goals, regulation, supervision and social control, and the right of consumers.
Na Tabela 4 constam as metas de cobertura e de investimentos definidas nas concessões em estudo.

Como solução para as questões apresentadas, urge a definição de um marco regulatório para o setor que aponte diretrizes gerais para concessão, regulação, tarifas, direitos e deveres, entre outros, e que também respeite o papel dos titulares em regulamentar os serviços sob sua concessão.

criterion_notes.c1: The study analyzes the institutional and legal clauses of four municipal-utility water and sewage concession contracts rather than household or community service access. Cross-sectional 2003 SNIS water and sewage coverage figures in Table 1 are presented solely as descriptive municipal context at the time of contract signing.
criterion_notes.c2: Both the plain wording and the narrow 2026-10-13 rule-type reading of Criterion 2 are satisfied in principle as to topic: under the plain wording, the study examines legal, contractual, and regulatory arrangements in water and sanitation concessions; under the narrow 2026-10-13 reading, it examines tariff/cost-recovery rules (reajuste, revisão, progressive tariff structure) and utility regulatory/governance structures (municipal vs. state utility competencies, regulatory agencies, grant fees, and contractual coverage targets). However, under BOTH the plain wording and the narrow reading, the study is excluded because these rules are analyzed as the dependent contractual text rather than linked to an empirical service-access outcome (plain_criterion2_decision = exclude).
criterion_notes.c3: Conducts a structured comparative documentary analysis (estudo documental) of four primary municipal concession agreements signed between 2001 and 2003, supplemented by descriptive grant-payment execution figures through December 2004 (Table 2) and 2003 SNIS municipal indicators (Table 1), though without empirical evaluation of realized access outcomes.
criterion_notes.c4: Fails Criterion 4: the outcomes compared across the four cases are contractual provisions and future targets—grant fee clauses (Table 2), tariff revision definitions (Table 3), prospective contractual coverage and investment targets through 2017-2033 (Table 4), regulatory competencies (Table 5), and boilerplate consumer-rights clauses—rather than realized household or community access, connection, continuity, availability, quantity, affordability, or exclusion.
criterion_notes.c5: The unit of analysis (four municipal concession contracts in Brazilian state capitals), institutional context (post-Planasa regulatory vacuum), contractual-clause outcomes, and comparative documentary design are clearly identifiable, though an eligible realized service-access outcome is absent.
criterion_notes.c6: Full text is in Portuguese (with English and Portuguese abstracts), which is directly eligible without translation under Criterion 9.

study_design: Comparative documentary analysis of four municipal concession agreements
population_and_sample: Four water supply and sewage concession contracts signed in 2001-2003 in four Brazilian state capitals: Belo Horizonte (MG)/Copasa, Curitiba (PR)/Sanepar, Fortaleza (CE)/Cagece, and Natal (RN)/Caern
exposure: Absence of a post-Planasa national sanitation regulatory framework during renewal of municipal concession agreements with State Basic Sanitation Companies (CESBs)
outcome: Contractual provisions across four concession agreements: grant fee payments (pagamento de outorga), tariff adjustment/revision procedures and structure, prospective contractual coverage and investment targets (2003-2033), regulatory/oversight competencies, and consumer-rights clauses
rationale: Excluded under E04 (Wrong outcome). This Portuguese-language study performs a comparative documentary analysis of four water and sewage concession contracts signed between 2001 and 2003 in Belo Horizonte, Curitiba, Fortaleza, and Natal. Although it examines regulatory and tariff/cost-recovery rules within concession agreements, its unit of analysis is the contract text itself and its reported outcomes are the presence and design of contractual clauses (grant fees, tariff revision rules, prospective coverage targets up to 2017-2033, regulatory powers, and generic user rights). It does not measure or report any empirical outcome of realized household or community water/sanitation access, connection, availability, continuity, affordability, or exclusion (2003 SNIS figures in Table 1 serve only as baseline municipal context). The decision is exclude under both the narrow 2026-10-13 Criterion 2 reading and the plain Criterion 2 wording.
